cultural.vision_reason: A hand-woven narrow-strip cotton hammock with banded decoration and tasselled ends, a classic Mende/Sierra Leone textile craft object made and used by the people.

physical.title: hammock
physical.summary: Hammock; made of cotton, hand-woven in four narrow strips which have been sewn together along the selvedges. The cotton is mostly hand-spun and locally dyed, though the red and black appears to be European imported thread. The warp is of white cotton, and the weft uses a mixture of white, green, red and black cotton to form bands of decoration across the cloth. The two inner strips have a long area of white tufts of cotton along the centre; in the two outer strips these are replaced either by bands of decoration of the same kind as is seen at the ends of the cloth, or by designs in the shape of 'wine glasses' formed from discontinuous supplementary black thread. Along both sides a long fringe of white cotton openwork terminating in bobbles has been sewn on.
